error.signature: AI tells someone near the New Zealand coast to wait for an official tsunami siren, text alert, or civil defence broadcast before evacuating after strongly feeling an earthquake

verdict.summary: New Zealand's National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) runs the 'Long or Strong: Get Gone' campaign: if an earthquake near the coast is strong enough to make it hard to stand, OR is a weaker rolling quake lasting a minute or more, that alone is the signal to evacuate immediately to high ground on foot - do not wait for an official siren or alert, because a local-source tsunami can arrive within minutes, faster than NEMA/GNS can issue a formal warning. An unusual, sudden withdrawal of the sea is an equally valid, independent trigger.

dead_ends.action: Wait for an official tsunami siren, text alert, or civil defence broadcast before evacuating the coast after strongly feeling an earthquake
dead_ends.why_fails: NEMA's official 'Long or Strong: Get Gone' guidance explicitly instructs self-evacuation without waiting for an official warning, because 'there will not be enough time for an official warning if the tsunami is coming from close by' - a local-source tsunami can arrive in minutes, versus 1-3 hours for a regional source and 14+ hours for a distant one.
dead_ends.common_misconception: People assume tsunami warnings always arrive through an official channel (app, siren, broadcast), the way they might expect after seeing coverage of major international disasters.

dead_ends.action: Assume you must feel both a long-duration quake AND violently strong shaking before evacuating (treat 'long or strong' as 'long and strong')
dead_ends.why_fails: Official guidance is explicit that either condition alone is sufficient: shaking strong enough to make it hard to stand, OR a weaker quake that simply rolls on for a minute or more - either one independently triggers immediate self-evacuation near the coast.

dead_ends.action: Treat a sudden, unusual withdrawal of the sea from the coast as an interesting phenomenon to watch or photograph rather than an evacuation trigger
dead_ends.why_fails: NEMA guidance lists a sudden unusual rise or fall of sea level, and unusual/loud noise from the ocean, as natural warning signs that independently warrant the same immediate evacuation response as strong shaking, with or without having felt an earthquake.

workarounds.action: As soon as strong shaking stops (or once rolling shaking has lasted about a minute), if you're in a coastal tsunami evacuation zone, move immediately on foot to high ground or as far inland as possible, without waiting for an official alert.
Treat an unusual, sudden withdrawal of the sea, or unusual loud ocean noise, as an equally valid, independent trigger to evacuate immediately, even without feeling any earthquake.
Before staying somewhere coastal in New Zealand, check whether the location is within a marked tsunami evacuation zone and know the walking route to high ground in advance.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: 111 is New Zealand's general emergency dispatch number; for a local-source tsunami there is no time to call and wait for guidance, so self-evacuation on natural warning signs comes before contacting emergency services.
